newsitem.title: UK: NWE heating oil cargo premiums firmer.
newsitem.headline: NWE heating oil cargo premiums firmer.

text.p: NWE heating oil cargo premiums were discussed slightly firmer on Thursday on colder weather and the emergence of possible arbitrage opportunities to Asia and the United States, traders said.
Sentiment also had a boost from the closure of two Indian refineries due to an oil pipeline burst, which stirred talk that Indian Oil Corp could make a second gas oil tender for January.

Benchmark Dec IPE futures firmed $2.75 to $219 a tonne following gains on NYMEX, in meagre volumes. Heating oil was offered at Dec IPE +$6 into Germany and offered at +$10 into Rostock. Russians were discussed at $1.50/2.50.
One major European trader fixed a gas oil cargo to India and others were exploring the same possibility.
Barges were moribund. German demand was scarce with bids at Dec IPE +$1.25/50 and sellers insisting on around Dec IPE +$2.
"Both sides are more than stubborn," one said. Some traders were sceptical of a report of a barge done fob Rotterdam at Dec IPE +$2.25.
Barge supply remained difficult because of absorption of capacity by the record high November IPE delivery.
Low sulphur barges were around Dec IPE +$12/13.
